bullets.title: LITE blowout Q4 FY26 earnings confirm optical demand inflection
bullets.body: Lumentum crosses $1B revenue for first time with Q4 FY26 at $1.006B (+109% YoY, +24.5% QoQ), non-GAAP EPS $3.23 beating $2.97 consensus, and gross margin at 50.4%. Management flagged unexpected demand surges in ultra-high-power lasers ('way behind on shipments'), scale-up CPO clarity for H2 2027, and initial ELS module orders—with Q1 guidance of $1.225–1.275B implying another ~24% sequential gain. Multiple accounts called it 'monster,' 'phenomenal,' and likely underpriced even in the $800s.

bullets.title: COHR Q4 FY26 beats across the board; first $3B+ quarter guided for June 2027
bullets.body: Coherent reported $2.05B revenue (+34% YoY) at top of guidance, with non-GAAP gross margin 40.2% and EPS $1.74 vs $1.58 consensus. Q1 guidance is $2.2–2.4B ($2.3B midpoint, ~12% sequential growth). Key call takeaway: Coherent moving upstream into InP substrate constraints and expanding into OCS, with FY27 essentially fully booked and purchase orders extending into 2028. Jefferies raised PT to $420.

bullets.title: NBIS reports 454% YoY revenue growth; $7–9B EoY ARR guided; Burry adds short
bullets.body: Nebius reported $582.3M Q2 revenue (+454% YoY, +46% QoQ) with ~50% adjusted EBITDA margins and $8B+ cash. 2026 full-year guidance raised to $3.0–3.4B. Concurrent with the blowout print, Michael Burry was disclosed to have doubled his NBIS short position—one commenter noted he called it 'shooting fish in a barrel.' The stock surged 34% (second-best day ever). Anthropic also signed a $9.1B deal with RIOT for GPU compute underpinning cloud demand.

bullets.title: NVDA $500B AI financing deal with Wall Street; Jensen frames GPUs as financeable assets
bullets.body: NVIDIA announced partnerships with Apollo, Blackrock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR to mobilize $500B+ in third-party capital for AI infrastructure customers. Jensen Huang explicitly framed the initiative as creating a new 'investable asset class'—noting A100 GPUs remain 'mission-capable' from 2020 through 2029. Critics called it a 'circle jerk SPV' masking weak FCF, while bulls saw it as the most significant AI financing structure in history. NVDA CDS spreads simultaneously widened to all-time highs near 80bps.

bullets.title: INTC $20B equity offering massively oversubscribed; CEO buys $12M personally
bullets.body: Intel upsized its equity offering to $20B (from $15B) after attracting $100B+ in demand at $95/share (~6.5% discount). CEO Lip-Bu Tan subscribed $12M personally. Analysts flagged 14A node gaining customer traction, Intel hinting at memory re-entry ('memory is no longer a commodity'), and GF Securities initiating Buy with $136 PT. Multiple accounts predicted NVDA, Google, Amazon, Microsoft, and AMD will eventually use Intel Foundry for CPU production.

bullets.title: UMich consumer sentiment crashes to 51.0 in August, well below 55.0 consensus
bullets.body: University of Michigan preliminary August sentiment fell to 51.0 from 55.2 in July, missing the 55.0 consensus by 400bps. Current conditions index at 51.8, expectations at 50.6. One-year inflation expectations ticked up to 4.3% from 4.2%. Partisan split noted: Republican confidence has fallen sharply since February's Iran war escalation. Score is approaching 2008 lows, though some question methodology changes. The Atlanta Fed simultaneously cut Q3 GDPNow to 4.3% from 5.8%.

bullets.title: July retail sales -0.6% MoM—largest monthly miss vs. expectations in recent memory
bullets.body: July retail sales came in at -0.6% MoM vs. +0.1% estimate and +0.2% prior, with ex-auto at -0.3%. Control group fell -0.4% vs. +0.4% prior. Goldman lowered Q3 GDP tracking by 50bps to 2.2%. Internet/nonstore retailers recorded the second-largest MoM decline since 2021. UBS noted fading OBBBA tax refund support as a risk factor. Futures briefly turned HOD on 'bad news is good news' narrative.

bullets.title: July CPI/PPI in-line: rate hike odds trimmed; market reads as 'dovish' print
bullets.body: July CPI rose 0.1% MoM / 3.4% YoY (consensus met) with core +0.2% / +2.5%. PPI printed 0.0% MoM vs. +0.2% consensus, core +0.2% vs. +0.3% est. September Fed rate hike odds fell from ~45% to 31-36% post-data. Goldman, Santander, and Baird all updated market-on-hold views. Cleveland's Hammack separately called for 'some number' of hikes, arguing current rates aren't meaningfully restrictive. 10-year Treasuries auctioned at highest yield since 2007 (4.683%), then 30-year at highest since 2001 (5.216%).

bullets.title: META +2.6% on open-weight Muse Glimmer release; internal LLM compute separation noted
bullets.body: Meta surged on releasing Muse Glimmer, a 30B open-weights model running on a single consumer GPU, plus announcing a $1B 'Future Is For Everyone Fund' for communities hosting data centers. Separately, one analyst flagged that most of Meta's compute spend goes to its internal LLM lab and should not be used to estimate long-term core margins—distinguishing Zuckerberg's 'abundance of jobs from AI' vision from the capex narrative. D1 Capital Q2 13F showed META as its top buy; META also appeared in Ackman's Pershing Square portfolio.

bullets.title: AAPL -2.5% on Jefferies downgrade to Underperform; glass iPhone canceled
bullets.body: Jefferies cut Apple to Underperform from Hold with a $263.66 PT, citing the 'roadmap to higher-priced iPhone looks challenging.' Simultaneously, The Information reported Apple canceled its planned all-glass 20th-anniversary iPhone ($2,600 ASP target) due to poor production yields. Apple also reported hiring Nate Gatten from American Airlines as VP of Government Affairs, and that AI writes 60% of company code (per CEO Chesky—note: that's Airbnb, not Apple). Memory is expected to represent 42% of iPhone 18 Pro BoM.

bullets.title: D1 Capital's Q2 13F: META as top buy; CRWV, TSLA new; AVGO, NVDA trimmed
bullets.body: Dan Sundheim's D1 Capital disclosed Q2 13F with new positions in CRWV, TSLA, and META (named top quarterly buy). D1 trimmed or exited AVGO and NVDA ('top sales'), and reduced CLS. CART remains the second-largest position at 3.07%. The filing tracks broader hedge fund rotation away from crowded semis and toward AI infrastructure plays directly accessible to capital.

bullets.title: SNDK Investor Day: 80% gross margin target; $93.9B backlog from 8 customers
bullets.body: SanDisk hosted investor day with CEO guiding mid-to-high teens revenue CAGR and 80% non-GAAP gross margins by FY2028–30, plus 50% adj. FCF margin. CFO disclosed $93.9B in total contract value from 8 customers over contract lives; plans to return 100% of excess cash to shareholders. Flash memory market projected to grow to $300B in 2026 and $500B in 2027. Meta is joining a consortium to develop an open HBF standard. Analyst noted SNDK shows 'sandbagging' on RPO calculations with upside potential.

bullets.title: CRWV surges 16–20% AH on Q2 beat: $2.58B revenue, $104B backlog, $25B new Q3 deals
bullets.body: CoreWeave posted Q2 revenue of $2.58B (doubling YoY), beating $2.56B estimate, with loss per share of -$1.14 vs. -$1.41 expected. Revenue backlog hit $104B at June 30; $25B+ in net new customer commitments were added in early Q3 (not in backlog). Cloud revenue beat at $126M; hardware revenue missed at $54M vs. $73M expected. One critical note: financing costs embedded in COGS and underlying B-rated bonds at 11% yield. Cerebras simultaneously missed Q2 revenue ($180M vs. $194M est.) and fell 17%.

bullets.title: SMCI blowout FY27 guidance: $65–72B revenue vs. $52B consensus; 9 customers >$1B
bullets.body: Super Micro Computer guided FY2027 net sales of $65–72B vs. $52.4B consensus, with Q1 guidance of $14.5–15.5B vs. $11.99B estimate. CFO disclosed 9 customers with revenue >$1B (up from 4 in FY25). Analyst called CEO 'a politician' for dodging specific margin guidance. $60B+ in new orders logged this earnings cycle. SpaceX/xAI cited as key tenant. JPMorgan raised PT to $45 from $32; MU EVP/CBO scheduled to present at upcoming summit.

bullets.title: TSMC July revenue +45% YoY to record $14.5B; capacity sold out at every node
bullets.body: TSMC reported July revenue of NT$467.58B ($14.5B), up 45% YoY with CoWoS yield clearing 99%. VP Jun He said TSMC is 'very close' to meeting CoWoS demand (not quite). Advanced packaging capacity has doubled annually for three years across ten fabs. TSM also approved a ¥1T ($6.3B) joint venture with Sony for image sensors targeting robots/AI. ABF substrates flagged as second-largest bottleneck after memory.

bullets.title: RDDT confirmed for S&P 500 inclusion August 18; stock had fallen 30% on earnings, then +15%
bullets.body: S&P Dow Jones Indices confirmed Reddit will replace AvalonBay in the S&P 500 prior to August 18 market open. The stock had plunged 30% on earnings two weeks prior, then rebounded 15% on the S&P inclusion news—move characterized as 'technicals, not fundamentals.' Reddit separately hired an experienced chief legal officer ('big hire').

bullets.title: NVDA Spectrum-X Ethernet Photonics enters full production; supply chain maps to LITE, COHR, TSM, FN
bullets.body: NVIDIA confirmed Spectrum-X Ethernet photonics scale-out networking is now in full production. Supply chain: TSM (SiPh fab/COUPE process), LITE (ELS/high-power lasers/optical alignment & test), COHR (ELS + optical components), GLW (fiber/connectors), FN (switch CPO assembly & test). The production announcement dispels CPO delay rumors; NVDA is simultaneously accelerating Feynman (H2 2028) on TSMC A16 with CPO integration.

bullets.title: MU: HBM demand strong; Goldman says memory is 62% of Vera Rubin BoM; structural LTAs confirmed
bullets.body: Multiple threads converged on bullish MU read-throughs: Goldman estimates memory at 62% of NVIDIA Vera Rubin BoM (with SOCAMM2 a larger-than-expected component). YMTC hitting 90% yield on 17nm DDR5 and achieving top-3 NAND is a competitive risk, but DRAM market revenue could hit $1T in 2027 alone (versus $1T cumulative 2010–2025). MU has 16+ long-term agreements with visibility into customer roadmaps beyond 2030. Server DDR5 prices rose 15–23% in August. Baillie Gifford and Renaissance both added MU in Q2.

bullets.title: 13F season highlights: Thrive buys AMZN ($215M), Baupost holds AMZN/GOOGL, Ackman adds NFLX
bullets.body: Key Q2 13F disclosures across window: Thrive Capital built $215M AMZN position (SpaceX dominant at 85%); Baupost largest position AMZN at $892M, GOOGL at $485M; Bill Ackman returned to NFLX ('dominant in its category') after a 2022 exit; Pat Dorsey holds $226M APP position; Renaissance sold MU/SNDK/AAPL/WDC but bought CRWD/META/NVDA/GOOGL/AMZN; TCI exited all MSFT in Q2; Leon Cooperman concentrated in VRT ($722M). Dodge & Cox holds $4.79B MSFT.

bullets.title: CSCO beats Q4 with +18% revenue growth; guides Q1 well above consensus
bullets.body: Cisco reported Q4 revenue of $17.3B (+18% YoY), beating $16.83B estimate, with non-GAAP EPS $1.22 (+23% YoY) vs. $1.17 expected. Q1 guidance of $18.0–18.2B crushed the $16.84B consensus; full-year 2027 EPS guided $5.05–5.11 vs. $4.84. AI infrastructure demand cited as primary growth driver. Melius raised CSCO PT to $160 from $145. One analyst noted Cisco simultaneously represents AI infrastructure exposure and scale-out optical competition to LITE/CIEN.
